children: Basis bids for soybeans shipped by barge to the U.S. Gulf Coast weakened on Wednesday and corn bids were mixed, amid a lack of fresh news on spot export demand and as the futures market saw choppy trading, traders said.

The National Weather Service is forecasting hotter-than-normal temperatures for most grain-growing areas over the next two weeks, while some areas are seeing a spate of rainfall that could delay corn harvests, traders said.
Strength in the U.S. dollar also weighed on export demand, as it makes already high-priced ag products more expensive for importers.
Chicago Board of Trade soybean futures rose on Wednesday and reached contract highs in deferred months on hopes of increased Chinese demand, as soymeal futures also set contract highs.

Traders waited to see whether top importer China would ramp up purchases of U.S. soybeans in conjunction with an expected meeting between Presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in Washington next week. On Tuesday, U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent disclosed plans to meet with his Chinese counterpart this weekend.
Freight values for empty barges have remained elevated with Gulf-area barge fleets starting to show signs of getting jammed up and delays building, barge sources said.

CIF soybean barges loaded in September were bid sharply lower for a second day, with bids down 6 cents at 79 cents over CBOT November (SX26) futures. October barges were bid at 95 cents over futures, down 3 cents.
FOB export premiums for Gulf soybean shipments in October were steady, offered at around 124 cents over November futures, while November shipments were offered at 127 cents over futures.

Bids for CIF corn barges were mixed, with September loadings bid 4 cents lower at 70 cents over CBOT December (CZ26) futures, while October barge bids ticked up 1 cent at 86 cents over December futures.

FOB export premiums for Gulf corn vessels loaded in the first half of October were also steady, offered at around 106 cents over December futures, while latter-half October were offered at 109 cents over December futures.
